info.title: ouroboros-rest (internal)
info.summary: What ouroboros-engine may ask the control plane for — and what it is never given.
info.description:
The **engine-facing** surface of
[Ouroboros](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros)' communications layer. Two
operations, one caller, and one idea holding both of them together — roadmap decision
**P3**, [#224](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/224):

> **A worker never holds a provider credential.**

Mockup 07's page subline promises something weaker — *"keys never leave the control
plane — workers only ever see short-lived tokens"* — and this document is where the
first clause is made literal and the second is **improved on**. There is no token. A
fifteen-minute credential is still a credential: it genuinely reaches the worker,
revocation is bounded only by its TTL, and the audit surface widens to every process
that ever held one. It is also, for most LLM providers, fiction — almost none support
deriving short-lived scoped keys, so such a token would in practice be a full API key
with a timer bolted on by us.

So the two operations divide the world:

| Operation | For | Hands over |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /internal/llm/invoke` | every **cloud** provider | nothing — the control plane makes the call and streams back the answer |
| `POST /internal/credentials/lease` | **local** providers only | an address, TTL-bounded and audited |

The exception is narrow and is not a compromise. An engine worker calling an Ollama
daemon on the same box gains nothing from proxying its traffic through this service,
because there is no key on that path to protect — so it is told the address and nothing
else, and a lease naming a cloud provider is a `403` by policy, enforced here rather
than trusted to the caller.

**What is built and what is specified.** The lease is implemented. The proxy is
*specified* by this document and implemented by AF.2
([#235](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/235)); calling it today answers
`501` with `code: "invocation_not_implemented"`, deliberately rather than `404`, so an
executor being written against this contract can tell *the path is right and the other
half is not built yet* from *I have the URL wrong*. The contract exists first because
AF.1 ([#234](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/234)) has to choose an
executor **against** it — a decision recorded afterwards is a description of whatever
got built.

**Authentication is the #51 pattern, in the other direction.** Every operation requires
`X-Ouro-Internal-Key`, carrying `OURO_ENGINE_SHARED_SECRET` — the same header and the
same variable `ouroboros-rest` sends when *it* calls the engine
([#51](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/51)). The comparison is constant
time, a missing header takes the same path as a wrong one, and the rejection is one
constant body: `401` with `code: "unauthenticated"` and nothing else. A session cookie
is not accepted here, whoever it belongs to.

**These paths are outside `/api`, and unversioned.** `/api` is the browser's boundary;
the only caller of these two is deployed alongside this service and upgraded with it, so
a version in the path would be one nobody could ever be on a different side of. That is
the same argument `/health/live` and `ouroboros-engine`'s `/healthz` are written under.

**Every error has the shape every other error in this system has** — `{code, message,
details}`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.3 — so a worker parses one envelope whether it
was refused at the boundary or inside a handler.

**The naming convention changes at this boundary, once.** This service writes
`camelCase` in its contracts and `ouroboros-engine` writes `snake_case` in its own; each
side translates in exactly one file — `src/modules/engine/engine.contract.ts` here,
`ouroboros_engine/control_plane/contract.py` there — so no code on either side carries
the other's spelling.

servers.description:
`yarn dev`. In a deployment this is the address the engine resolves the control plane
at — `http://rest:4000` inside the compose network — which is never the address a
browser uses.

tags.name: credentials
tags.description:
**What a worker is given, and what it is not.**

One operation, and its shape is the argument. A lease carries an address, a run, a
workspace and two timestamps — there is no field for a secret, which is how *no secret
is ever returned* is enforced by the type rather than by a test that inspects a payload
and hopes it looked everywhere. A lint rule
(`src/modules/internal/no-secret-responses.mjs`) refuses one added later.

A lease is **not a bearer token.** Possessing one grants nothing that knowing the
address would not, which is why nothing stores it and there is no way to revoke one.
What the TTL bounds is how long a worker should keep believing the answer before asking
again — real staleness, not theatrical security. Calling a fifteen-minute expiry on a
hostname a security control is the kind of claim `docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md`
([#226](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/226)) exists to keep out of the
product.

tags.name: invocation
tags.description:
**The proxy — specified here, implemented by AF.2
([#235](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/235)).**

The worker sends the call it wants made and the run it is making it for; the control
plane resolves the target, unwraps the credential inside one request scope, walks the
resolved chain and streams back what the provider said. The key never crosses back.

One choke point rather than a policy in every worker is what makes AB.1's
([#207](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/207)) semantics implementable at
all: the per-hop error taxonomy, the floor that a chain may not degrade past, the
per-run cost cap, and usage capture attributed to the hop that actually served the
request. Each of those is a field or an event kind below, named here so that an
executor which ignored one can be found to have ignored it.

post.summary: Lease a local provider's address for one run
post.description:
Tell a worker where a **local** provider is, for the duration of one run.

Three refusals, in this order, and the order is part of the contract:

1. **`403 provider_not_leasable`** — the provider is one whose credentials never
   leave the control plane. Applied before anything is looked up, so no
   configuration and no state can produce a grant. `anthropic`, `copilot` and
   `cursor` are refused here; use `POST /internal/llm/invoke` instead.
2. **`404 local_provider_not_configured`** — a leasable kind this deployment has not
   been told the address of. An absence, not a decision: an operator fixes it by
   setting `OURO_LOCAL_PROVIDER_URLS`. A worker should not retry.
3. **`404 run_not_found`** — no such run, so there is nothing to scope the lease to.

The workspace a grant is audited against is **resolved from the run**, never taken
from the request: a worker naming its own workspace would be a worker choosing which
one to be audited against. Every grant writes a `credential.lease_granted` event
carrying the lease, the run, the workspace, the provider and the address — never
secret material, because on this path there is none.

`200` rather than `201`: nothing is created, nothing is stored, and there is no URL
to `GET` afterwards.

200.description:
The lease. An address and nothing else — inspect the payload: there is no field
in which a credential could arrive.

401.description:
No `X-Ouro-Internal-Key`, or the wrong one. One constant body: `code:
"unauthenticated"`, a bare message and empty `details`, whichever it was.

403.description:
`provider_not_leasable` — a cloud provider's credentials never leave the control
plane. This is policy, not state: no configuration makes it a `200`.

example.message: This provider is reached through the invocation proxy; its credentials never leave the control plane. Call POST /internal/llm/invoke instead.

404.description:
`local_provider_not_configured` — this deployment declares no provider of that
kind — or `run_not_found`.

example.message: This deployment has no local provider of that kind. Set OURO_LOCAL_PROVIDER_URLS to declare one.

422.description:
`validation_failed` — `provider` is not one of the five kinds, `run` is not a
uuid, or the body carries a field this operation does not define. `details` has
one entry per field refused.

example.message: The request body is not valid.

provider: provider must be one of the following values: ollama, openai_compatible, anthropic, copilot, cursor

post.summary: Ask the control plane to make a model call (specified — AF.2 implements it)
post.description:
Make a model call on the worker's behalf and stream the answer back.

**Not implemented.** This operation is specified by AD.3
([#224](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/224)) and implemented by AF.2
([#235](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/235)); it answers `501
invocation_not_implemented` today. The `200` below is the contract AF.2 is being
built against, and it is described here rather than after the fact because AF.1
([#234](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/234)) has to choose between a
custom executor and LiteLLM-as-executor *against a written contract*.

**The target is `connection` or `alias`, exactly one.** A connection is a concrete
provider connection and means *this provider and no other*. An alias means *whatever
routing resolves it to*, which is an ordered chain with a floor and a cap — resolved
by Z.1 ([#194](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/194)) **on this side** of
the boundary, so that a worker cannot send a chain other than the one routing chose.

**`payload` is opaque and passes through.** The adapters own the per-provider shape;
this service brokers the call and does not read the prompt.

**The answer is always a stream** — `application/x-ndjson`, one event per line — even
when the provider did not stream. Two response shapes would be two code paths, and
the non-streaming one would be the one that quietly stopped emitting usage. NDJSON
rather than SSE because the reader is a worker process, not a browser: reconnection
and event ids buy nothing here and cost a framing layer on both sides.

**Every AB.1 ([#207](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/207)) semantic has
a name in this contract** — `floorHopIndex`, `costCapCents`, the `usage` event, the
`hop` event and the error codes with their per-hop rules. They are hooks: this
document says what they mean, AF.1 decides how they are implemented, AF.2 implements
them.

200.description:
The stream. One JSON object per line, terminated by a `done` or an `error` event.

**Specified, not yet answered** — see the operation description and the `501`
below.

401.description:
No `X-Ouro-Internal-Key`, or the wrong one. Checked before anything else, so an
unauthenticated caller learns nothing about what this path will one day do.

501.description:
`invocation_not_implemented` — the contract is published and AF.2
([#235](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/235)) is what makes it
answer. Deliberately not a `404`, which is what a caller with the wrong path
gets.

example.message: The invocation proxy is specified and not yet implemented. It lands with AF.2 (issue #235); this route exists so the contract can be built against.

ouroInternalKey.name: X-Ouro-Internal-Key
ouroInternalKey.description:
The shared secret both sides read from `OURO_ENGINE_SHARED_SECRET`
([#51](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/51)). It is a **deployment**
credential, not a caller's: it says *this request came from inside*, and says nothing
about who or what sent it. Compared in constant time; a missing header and a wrong
one are the same answer.

The same header `ouroboros-rest` sends when it calls `ouroboros-engine`, so a stack
where the two values disagree fails in both directions at once — which is the failure
an operator can actually find.

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The body of **every** error on this surface — the same shape the public API and
`ouroboros-engine` answer with (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` § 5.3), so a worker parses one
envelope whether it was refused at the boundary or inside a handler.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable, and the thing to branch on.

message.description:
Written for a person. It never names anything about the service's own internals,
and a rejection at the boundary is one constant sentence whatever earned it.

details.description:
Whatever is specific to this failure — the provider that was refused, the run that
was not found, the field messages of a `422`. Always present, empty rather than
absent, so a client reading `details.provider` never has to check `details` first.

ProviderKind.title: ProviderKind
ProviderKind.description:
A provider kind — AC.1's ([#216](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/216))
registry keys, spelled as `ouroboros-db` writes them in
`model_prices.match_provider_kind`.

`ollama` and `openai_compatible` are **leasable**: both are reached without a
credential, which is what makes an address worth handing over. The other three are
**proxied**: there is nothing useful to lease, because the part that matters is the
key.

`openai_compatible` is leasable with a caveat worth reading, because the same adapter
fronts a vLLM on somebody's own GPU **and** `api.openai.com`. Nothing at the level of
a kind can tell those apart — local-ness is a property of the *connection* — so a
lease for it still fails unless the deployment has declared where that provider is.
The operator's declaration is the connection-level statement, made once at deployment
level until Y.1 ([#189](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/189)) makes it a
row.

LeaseRequest.title: LeaseRequest
LeaseRequest.description:
What a worker asks for: a provider kind, and the run it is working on.

A *kind* rather than a connection id, because there are no connections yet — Y.1
([#189](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/189)) brings them. Cloud kinds
are accepted **by the validator** and refused by the policy with `403`, deliberately:
a `422` would say *there is no such provider* about a provider the product supports.

run.description:
The run this work belongs to — `runs.id`. What *scoped* means: the workspace the
grant is audited against is resolved from it.

Lease.title: Lease
Lease.description:
A granted lease. **Every field is an identifier, an address or a timestamp** — there
is nowhere for a secret to be, which is the acceptance criterion *no secret, verified
by payload inspection* expressed as a shape rather than as a test.

`baseUrl` and no `host`: publishing both would be publishing one fact twice, in two
spellings that can disagree, where the lossier one is the one a client would have to
reassemble a URL from.

id.description: This grant's id — the same value the `credential.lease_granted` event carries.

run.description: The run it is scoped to, echoed so an answer can be matched to its request.

organizationId.description:
The workspace that run belongs to, resolved rather than supplied. Published
because the worker has to attribute what it does next — usage, telemetry — to the
same workspace this grant was audited against.

baseUrl.description: Where the provider is. The whole of what is handed over.

expiresAt.description: When the worker should ask again.

ttlSeconds.description:
How long that is — 900. It bounds **staleness**, not exposure: a lease carries no
secret, so there is nothing an expiry could revoke.

RunContext.title: RunContext
RunContext.description:
The run a call is made for — *per-run scoping*, as a shape. Everything about a call
that is not the call: whose work it is, where it sits in a chain, and the two limits
that may stop it.

The worker supplies what it knows; the control plane is the authority on the rest. A
cap a worker sent that is looser than the workspace's is not the cap that applies.

run.description:
The run — `runs.id`. Required: a call that belongs to no run cannot be
attributed.

hop.description:
Which hop of the resolved chain this is, zero-based. Normally absent: walking the
chain is the control plane's job, not the worker's.

stage.description:
The workflow stage — `runs.stage_label`. Telemetry rather than policy: AB.2
([#208](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/208)) is what makes *which
stage was running* the thing that renders a spike legible.

floorHopIndex.description:
The hop index below which the chain may not degrade — AB.1's floor, and mockup
06's *"never silently below the floor you set"*. Exhausting the chain down to it
fails the run with `floor_exhausted` rather than using a hop beneath it.

costCapCents.description:
The per-run spend ceiling, in cents. Checked pre-flight **and** while running: a
single streamed response can cross a cap it was under when it started.

resolutionVersion.description:
Which resolution this call was planned against — Z.1's `resolution_version`. It
crosses the boundary so that a call planned under one resolution and executed
after a rebind is recognisable as such.

vote.description:
Is this a vote rather than the primary call? `add_vote` escalation is a real
invocation with its own usage, and marking it is what keeps a vote's tokens from
inflating what the primary call cost.

InvokeRequest.title: InvokeRequest
InvokeRequest.description:
What the worker is asking the control plane to do. Exactly one of `connection` or
`alias`; the credential is not among the fields, because the worker does not have one.

connection.description:
A concrete provider connection — `provider_connections.id` (Y.1). *This provider*:
no chain, no fallback, no floor.

alias.description:
A routing alias — `model_aliases.alias` (Y.1). *Whatever routing resolves this
to*, which is an ordered chain with a floor and a cap.

payload.description:
The model call itself, in the adapter's own vocabulary. Opaque: nothing in this
service reads it, which is also why nothing in this service can log it.

InvokeEvent.title: InvokeEvent
InvokeEvent.description:
One line of the streamed answer. Five kinds, and between them they carry everything
AB.1 requires an executor to report: what the model said, what it cost, what each hop
did, and how it ended.

A stream ends with exactly one terminal event — `done` or `error`.

InvokeErrorCode.title: InvokeErrorCode
InvokeErrorCode.description:
The per-hop error taxonomy — AB.1's rules, named, with the behaviour each one implies.
#235's first acceptance criterion is that an executor's failover matches *what
routing's explanation promised the user*, so the mapping lives in the contract both
sides read rather than inside whichever module walks the chain.

| Code | What it is | What the executor does |
|---|---|---|
| `provider_unavailable` | 5xx or a timeout | advances to the next hop |
| `provider_rate_limited` | 429 or a provider throttle | backs off, then advances |
| `provider_auth_failed` | the credential was refused | does **not** retry; marks the provider in error |
| `request_invalid` | a 4xx that is not auth | aborts — the next hop would refuse it too |
| `floor_exhausted` | the chain reached its floor | aborts with the floor reason |
| `cost_cap_exceeded` | the run's cap is spent | aborts, naming the cap |
| `chain_exhausted` | every hop failed, no floor to stop at | aborts |

InvokeDeltaEvent.title: InvokeDeltaEvent
InvokeDeltaEvent.description: A streamed fragment of the model's answer.

hop.description: Which hop produced it — a chain that failed over says so in the stream.

text.description: The fragment, exactly as the provider sent it.

InvokeUsageEvent.title: InvokeUsageEvent
InvokeUsageEvent.description:
What one hop cost — the row `token_usage`
([#66](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/66)) gets. Emitted **per hop**,
including a hop that failed partway, attributed to the model and provider that
actually served it: a fallback hop's tokens attributed to the primary is every spend
number in the product subtly wrong in a way nobody notices for months.

connection.description: The provider connection that served it.

model.description: The model as the provider names it.

costCents.description:
What it cost, or `null` when nothing prices it. `null` rather than `0` — the
honesty rule CH.3 ([#586](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/586))
already enforces: a local model's tokens are *unpriced*, which is a different
statement from *free*, and a zero here is spend nobody incurred appearing in an
aggregate.

InvokeHopEvent.title: InvokeHopEvent
InvokeHopEvent.description:
A hop finished, one way or another — the telemetry AB.2
([#208](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/issues/208)) aggregates. Emitted for
every hop *attempted*, so a chain that failed over twice produces three of them and a
reader can see the failover the routing explanation promised.

latencyMs.description: How long the attempt took — AB.2's latency input.

InvokeErrorEvent.title: InvokeErrorEvent
InvokeErrorEvent.description: The invocation failed. Terminal — no further events follow.

hop.description: Which hop was in flight, when one was.

message.description:
A sentence for a person. Never a provider's own error text: those are not this
API's contract and have carried tokens before now.

InvokeDoneEvent.title: InvokeDoneEvent
InvokeDoneEvent.description: The invocation completed. Terminal — no further events follow.

hop.description: Which hop served the answer — the one the run should be attributed to.

finishReason.description: Why generation stopped, in the provider's own vocabulary.
